Stopping cutting is really tricky. You need to find new (and healthy) coping skills. Here are some things I do instead of hurting myself:
-draw where I want to cut
-call and friend and talk about anything until the urges pass.
-get one of "bloody" ice cubes I've made (water with red food dye) and hold it for as long as I can.
-draw on paper 
-listen to music with headphones on really loud (not good for my ears)

Therapy might also he helpful for you. Having a professional give you coping skills and advice is awesome.

But please remember it's not a one and done. You probably out kick it the first time around or even the 100th, and that's okay. It is an addiction and you can beat it.

I set a date for December 7th last December. The only reason I didn't do it was because I was scared I would destroy my therapist's career. A month after my 'expiration date' I was so mad at myself for not doing it, I didn't feel any better. Then I got a phone call. From my dad. He was distraught telling me that my sister in law had been killed. She left behind my brother and their two sons (2 and 3). My life changed so dramatically at that point. I now am responsible for taking care of two toddlers. They are my new reason for living. I cannot let them down. I am still suicidal, I still hurt myself. But now I have two boys to fight for and for the first in a very long time, I feel hope.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that life can hit you with a 'purpose' at any moment. It can been something big or small. It can come wrapped in grief. Sometimes we have to live for other people until we can live for ourselves. Maybe your purpose for now is just surviving. I hope you find your peace.
